historical_reviews.v3_1: This is an AC-input-path behavior test, not merely a PSU-presence check. For each mapped cord, acceptance must distinguish input-loss detection, chassis power transition, BMC survivability, SEL identity and restored PSU LED; the explicit power-off criterion cannot be silently replaced by a redundant-power expectation.

original_test_intent: Validate each PSU input cord's removal and restoration behavior, including the source-specified SUT power-off response, PSU-specific SEL events and LED recovery.
original_method: Map every PSU to its inlet and AC feed, approve the expected one-cord outage semantics, preserve a complete powered baseline, have an authorized operator remove exactly one mapped cord, timestamp chassis/BMC reachability and PSU/SEL state, reconnect the same cord, then prove the approved boot/power and LED recovery before moving to another feed.
manual_activity: A power owner approves the platform-specific single-cord power-off oracle and outage/recovery plan; an authorized operator removes and restores each cord and an observer verifies its LED.
required_inputs: Approved interpretation of the single-cord power-off criterion
Expected BMC behavior during chassis power loss
PSU LED recovery state and deadline
safety_requirements: Do not handle AC hardware remotely or by automation
Confirm cord identity at both ends
Remove only one approved cord at a time
Drain workloads before an expected outage
Do not assume redundant survival contrary to the source
Stop on arcing, wrong feed, abnormal PSU state or recovery failure
Do not continue to the next PSU until full recovery
agent_execution_scope: Verify the approved PSU/feed map and expected power semantics
Capture complete baseline power, PSU, SEL and reachability state
Timestamp read-only BMC and console evidence around the operator action
Correlate input-loss and recovery records to the selected PSU
Verify approved post-reconnect power and management recovery
engineer_actions: Approve workload outage and AC procedure
Perform or supervise cord handling and LED observation
Authorize any manual power-on needed after reconnect
Stop further PSU iterations after unexpected behavior

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The proposed grep/tail snapshots can support PSU and SEL observation but cannot prove the source-required outage, correct feed identity, BMC survival or full recovery, and truncation may omit the relevant events.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use approved read-only BMC/Redfish/IPMI and independent console/reachability monitoring around a single operator-controlled cord removal and restoration; preserve complete per-PSU events rather than tailing a fixed count.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Each installed PSU cord remains in scope and the 5-minute estimate is preserved, subject to the approved recovery deadline and one-at-a-time gating.

modernized_recommendation.status: TOPOLOGY-BOUND SINGLE-CORD OUTAGE AND RECOVERY MATRIX
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: For each PSU input, record feed identity, pre-state, exact removal time, chassis/BMC behavior, PSU-specific SEL transition, reconnection, required power-on action and LED/health stabilization.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit feed topology, outage authorization, BMC-survival expectations and complete recovery checkpoints without changing the source's power-off oracle.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A final PSU-good snapshot cannot show whether the correct feed was removed, whether the chassis powered off as specified, or whether recovery required an unrecorded intervention.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Live AC removal can interrupt the whole host, lose data or management access, and an unexpected redundant or nonredundant topology can make the source oracle unsafe or inapplicable.

project_override_considerations: The owner must state whether every installed PSU shares a nonredundant dependency or whether the source's `powered-off` criterion is an intentional platform exception; the review must not silently convert it to `remain powered-on` from the adjacent case.
expected_evidence: Approved PSU/cord/feed map, topology and exact power-off oracle
SUT/BMC/firmware identity, workload/outage authorization, operator/observer and timestamps
Complete per-PSU baseline, input-loss and restoration sensor/SEL data
Chassis, OS, console and BMC reachability/power timeline
PSU LED visual evidence and any manual power-on action
Stable final health, preserved logs, no-repeat audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source Procedure specifies the physical operation and Criteria explicitly supplies the power-off oracle; no source field states that the SUT must remain on. The result is unusual for an all-PSU population and therefore requires platform confirmation, but it is not an internal contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target, physical action and stated acceptance are identifiable. Execution is conditional on topology, outage approval and recovery inputs, so REQUIRES is appropriate rather than BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Preserves the source's atypical outage expectation while turning each cord cycle into an auditable feed-specific power, management, SEL and LED transition with controlled recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: Removing one cord tests an AC feed path, not simply whether a PSU object disappears from inventory. If the chassis is expected to shut down, the evidence must separate graceful or abrupt host loss from BMC auxiliary-power behavior and must identify how the system returns after AC is restored. Otherwise a later green LED can conceal a wrong-feed operation, an unobserved data-loss event or an unsupported manual recovery step.
